title: Minimum Bit Flips to Reach Target XOR
description: You are given a 0-indexed array of non-negative integers `nums` and a non-negative integer `k`. In a single operation, you may choose any element of `nums` and flip any one bit in its binary representation (changing a 0 to 1 or a 1 to 0). Return the minimum number of operations required to make the bitwise XOR of all elements in `nums` equal to `k`.
hints: Flipping bit `b` of any single element in `nums` flips bit `b` of the overall XOR of `nums`.
Compute `diff = (XOR of all nums) ^ k`; each set bit in `diff` requires exactly one bit flip.

examples.explanation: Current XOR is 2^1^3^4 = 4 (100), target k = 1 (001); they differ in 2 bit positions.
Current XOR is 2^0^2^0 = 0, which already equals k = 0, so 0 flips are needed.
Current XOR is 0 and target k = 7 (111), requiring 3 bit flips.
